correctness.rationale: For every n>=1, Kasteleyn signs give det K=±W. The signed matrix reduces modulo two to U⊗V of rank \(n^2\) in size \(n(n+1)\), implying uniform \(2^n\) divisibility. Deleting diagonal n rows/columns leaves an odd determinant: a vector supported off the deleted columns with image supported on deleted rows must vanish by binary row sums and the explicit Kronecker kernel. The top controlled-sign finite difference divided by \(2^n\) is odd, so an odd number attain exact valuation n. Walsh inversion excludes odd gcd divisors. The standalone exact checker tests rank/minor through n=12, match-sums through n=5, Kasteleyn determinants through n=4.

originality.rationale: The universal \(2^n\) lower bound is implied by Barkley–Liu Lemma 2.9 and Example 6.10, since every signed Kasteleyn determinant has the same binary rank; that lower-bound mechanism is expressly not claimed as new. The additional exact all-order attainability, odd parity of minimal-valuation signings on a designated diagonal edge set, and hence exact Walsh gcd \(2^n\) were not identified in inspected primary sources or searchable mathematical records. A novel odd complementary-minor proof is given.
residual_risks: An overlooked all-signed gcd formula may exist in historical statistical-mechanics or integral matrix literature.
A general Kasteleyn determinant method covers the algebraic representation; historical novelty is restricted to the exact all-order gcd, explicit minor, and odd witness parity.
No independent referee or external proof certification has been performed.

value.rationale: Known unsigned Aztec tilings have valuation \(n(n+1)\)/2, and known channels give a universal signed determinant lower bound n. The proved exact common Walsh divisor shows this barrier is attained in every order; a natural n-edge flip family contains an odd number of sharp signings. This closes an all-order arithmetic attainability question for natural planar dimers, rather than recomputing one positive partition function.
